A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of forgetting through example-association matrices. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning measurements, association analyses, forgetting-prediction results, and replay experiments, including Tables 1–3 and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports original association measurements, similarity correlations, prediction results, and replay experiments across expanded settings, including Tables 1–2 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The core approach remains association-matrix analysis, additive/SVD/KNN completion using 30 seed examples, and exponentially weighted replay. v2 explains the existing KNN predictor more fully. Replay frequency and temperature changes are experimental settings rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Dolly instruction tasks and RedPajama upstream evaluation while retaining the earlier FLAN/Tulu, Dolma, MMLU, BBH, and TruthfulQA coverage. Replay evaluation expands beyond v1's FLAN-to-Dolma experiment to out-of-domain Tulu/Dolly tasks and preservation of instruction-tuning data.

E2.justification: v2 adds MIR, PPL, and gradient-based selection for OLMo-1B to the replay comparisons, retaining random replay and ground-truth weighting (Figure 6). The prediction comparator families remain: v1's Rep-dot is renamed Similarity, not newly added. The explicit trained no-replay score from v1 Table 3 is absent from the corresponding v2 comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds OLMo-1B and MPT-7B target models and full-parameter fine-tuning settings. Replay changes from one example per update with temperature 0.2 to eight examples every 32 updates with temperature 0.1. Prediction drops F1; new analyses use Spearman correlations, and replay tests specify 10,000 held-out examples. The stated 625/37 LoRA update budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New Section 3.3 tests whether textual similarity and gradient-based approximations explain forgetting, using correlations and matrix visualizations (Table 1, Figure 8). SVD analyses expand across full tuning and LoRA configurations. Conversely, v1 Table 1's separate upstream-only and task-only additive fits are omitted.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 reports means and standard deviations; v2 shows means only, despite Appendix B still claiming standard deviations are reported. Ten repetitions remain documented for in-domain prediction. Replay retains paired t-tests but replaces exact p-values with significance thresholds. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Prediction and association results expand across model/tuning configurations, while F1 and appendix per-task forgetting statistics disappear. New similarity correlations are 0.004, 0.005, and -0.007 (v2 Table 1). v1's KNN replay result was nonsignificant, p=0.1600; v2 reports significance in four of five setups. Changed protocols and coverage prevent treating these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds first-order gradient-based approximations, a random-projection preservation argument, and explicit truncated-SVD reconstruction and optimality statements (Sections 3.2–3.3). These are limited mathematical additions without a new proof framework. The new statement that SVD minimizes R2 conflicts with the retained R2 definition.

C1.justification: The low-rank association and matrix-completion claims remain. v2 adds the main finding that common similarity measures poorly predict forgetting and elevates efficient replay mitigation to an explicit contribution. Its abstract and introduction now claim statistically significant mitigation, beyond v1's nonsignificant practical demonstration.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving failure of first-order approximations, differences between data importance and forgettability, and MIR's limited candidate pool. It explicitly identifies the two-fine-tuning-run overhead and when this remains practical. Much previous limitations discussion moves into related work, while the qualification that forgetting can be desirable is removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents full-tuning schedules, five SVD latent features, and revised replay minibatches. However, it removes v1's optimizer and GPU specifications, per-task sample counts, upstream statistics table, and plan to release code/statistics upon acceptance. The project link remains; the PDFs do not establish any actual change in external resource availability.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating existing discussion, v2 substantially develops positioning against task-similarity theory, data selection, and replay research. Additions include Doan, Ding, Evron, Ostapenko, and Aljundi, with explicit distinctions from their settings and notions of importance. Jin and Ren's preprint-to-publication update represents the same prior work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the exposition are rewritten. Setup and prediction sections gain a more detailed subsection structure, association analyses are reorganized, and much limitations material moves into related work. The standalone ethical considerations and acknowledgements disappear.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a single-column layout, adds setup and prediction diagrams, expands heatmaps and SVD displays, replaces the replay table with a five-panel plot, and restructures appendix task tables. Figure 7 introduces contradictory captions describing LoRA as full tuning and RedPajama as Dolma.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited experimental generality and weak practical validation through broader model/tuning/corpus comparisons, additional replay baselines, and held-out evaluations reporting significant benefits in four of five setups. The similarity analysis also tests an important alternative explanation. These gains outweigh the loss of prediction standard deviations and some reproducibility details, although those omissions and the mathematical/caption errors remain weaknesses.
